Profit, Fees and Break-Even

Fees are taken twice: once when you buy and again when you sell. A trade can look profitable on price alone and still lose money once both fees are paid. The break-even price shows exactly where the line is.

Crypto prices can fall as fast as they rise. Check the Bitcoin Signal Today for the current trend before you decide anything, and never invest money you cannot afford to lose.

Questions & Answers

How do I calculate crypto profit?

Divide the amount invested (after the buy fee) by the buy price to get the coins you own. Multiply by the sell price, take off the sell fee, and subtract what you invested. The difference is your profit or loss.

What is the break-even price?

It is the sell price at which you get back exactly what you invested once both fees are paid. Selling above it is a profit, below it a loss.

What fees should I enter?

Use your exchange's trading fee, often 0.1% to 1.5% per trade. Card purchases and instant-buy buttons are usually more expensive than the exchange's own order book.

Does this include tax?

No. Tax on crypto gains depends on your country. Use the profit figure here as the starting point for your own tax calculation.
